List the registered fit functions

Source: R/fit_fn_registry.R
get_fit_fns.Rd

The fit functions known to this session, with the description each one carries, for presenting a choice.

Usage

get_fit_fns(data_type = NULL)

Arguments

data_type

character vector; keep only functions written for these profiles. NULL keeps all.

Value

data.frame, one row per registered function, with columns name, package, fn_name, data_type (comma separated), model, description, reference and available. Zero rows when nothing matches.

Details

A function is listed as unavailable when its package is not installed, or when its available predicate returns FALSE — a fit needing Python is registered but not offered on a machine without it.

model, description and reference are read from the attributes set_fit_fn_info attaches, and are NA for a function that does not carry them.

Providers register when they load

An entry exists only once the package registering it has been loaded, so a fit function from another package is missing from this table until then. Call requireNamespace() on the packages you care about first if you need the full catalogue.

See also

register_fit_fn, get_fit_profiles

Examples

get_fit_fns()
#>                           name  package                      fn_name
#> 1    fit_drug_response_metrics gDRutils    fit_drug_response_metrics
#> 2 fit_drug_response_metrics_4p gDRutils fit_drug_response_metrics_4p
#> 3              gompertz_fit_fn gDRutils              gompertz_fit_fn
#> 4              hormesis_fit_fn gDRutils              hormesis_fit_fn
#> 5                   ll3_fit_fn gDRutils                   ll3_fit_fn
#> 6                   ll5_fit_fn gDRutils                   ll5_fit_fn
#> 7              weibull1_fit_fn gDRutils              weibull1_fit_fn
#> 8              weibull2_fit_fn gDRutils              weibull2_fit_fn
